clue.text: Section reserved for reviews

parts.note: a newspaper's page set aside for critics' write-ups of plays, books and films, named for what those write-ups are called

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor marks off a part of the paper just for critics.
explanation.walkthrough: Critics' reviews are also called notices, and the page or column of announcements in a paper bears the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviews of a play or book are traditionally called notices, so the part of the paper holding them carries that name.

clue.text: It may be held in revulsion

definitions.text: It may be held in revulsion

parts.words: It may be held in revulsion
parts.note: reads as something regarded with disgust; really what you pinch shut when faced with a foul smell

explanation.surface: Something that is regarded with loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in revulsion' sounds like 'held in contempt'; literally it is gripped between fingers against a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: People pinch this facial feature shut when disgusted by a bad smell.

clue.text: A row about it mounts

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters climb upwards, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A quarrel concerning something escalates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A row' looks like an argument but is a line of seats; 'mounts' reverses RE and IT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row, as one of a series of rows of seats rising one above another.

clue.text: Spotted animals involved in the chase

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up and twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Spotted big cats take part in a pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges THE CHASE; 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheetahs are big cats with spotted coats, famous for speed in the hunt.

clue.text: Set up works of deception

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for works is set upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: OPS, plural of OP, short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone stages deliberately misleading productions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works of deception' reads as one phrase, but 'of' is a piece in its own right and 'deception' alone is the definition; 'Set up' means upwards in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a hoax or trick, a piece of deception.

clue.text: Cut by a quarter? That's serious

parts.note: to cut through is to sever
E, east, is one of the four quarters or cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether reducing something by a quarter counts as a grave measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut by a quarter' suggests taking away 25 per cent; instead the quarter is a compass point, E, set beside SEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a severe illness or problem is a serious one.

clue.text: Tax cut

definitions.meaning: a duty levied on goods, especially home-produced ones
to remove surgically or cut out

explanation.surface: A tax reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a duty on goods, and to excise is to cut something out.

clue.text: Gets rid of junk in sale time

indicators.note: to junk is to throw away, so these words are scrapped and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A shop clears out rubbish during its sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' looks like the thing being cleared out but signals rearranging IN SALE TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to eliminate is to get rid of or remove completely.

clue.text: Sound indication that a watch is fully wound up?

definitions.text: Sound indication that a watch is fully wound up?

parts.words: Sound indication that a watch is fully wound up?
parts.note: reads as a timepiece wound fully; really the ringing at sea that signals a ship's watch, a duty period, has come to an end

explanation.surface: A clicking noise shows a wristwatch has been wound completely.
explanation.walkthrough: On ships, a bell is struck every half hour of a four-hour watch; the final ring marks the watch 'wound up', that is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: At sea, the bell struck eight times signals the end of a four-hour watch.

clue.text: Sort of key found in a cupboard?

definitions.meaning: a master key that opens many locks has this name
the idiom of a shameful secret kept hidden, the bones in the cupboard

explanation.surface: A puzzled householder wonders what kind of key turned up in the cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key opens many locks, and a family's shameful secret is the proverbial bones in the cupboard.

clue.text: Taking part temporarily

definitions.meaning: performing a role on stage, playing a part
standing in for a while, as a deputy holding a post until someone permanent is appointed

explanation.surface: Someone joins in for a short while only.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a part on stage is acting, and a stand-in head is an acting head, holding the job temporarily.

clue.text: Breaks a leg, has to play on without a pause

indicators.note: the letters of the words are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: An actor told to break a leg must carry on performing without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' rearranges A LEG; TO is added as written, and 'has' links. 'Break a leg' is theatre's good-luck wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction to play smoothly, the notes joined with no pause between them.

clue.text: Packed garment for a self-important personage

parts.note: filled tightly, as stuffed
a shirt is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A tightly packed piece of clothing is likened to a pompous dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a pompous, self-important person is called a stuffed shirt.

clue.text: Measures not intended to be taken seriously?

definitions.text: Measures not intended to be taken seriously?

parts.words: Measures not intended to be taken seriously?
parts.note: measures read as steps or policies; really metrical lines of poetry written to amuse

explanation.surface: Policies that are not meant to be taken seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measures' suggests actions or quantities; in poetry a measure is a metre, so the lines are humorous poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Light verse is humorous poetry, written in metrical measures for amusement.

clue.text: Bird catchers' practical jokes?

parts.note: a booby is a tropical seabird
traps are devices that catch

explanation.surface: Bird-catchers' snares described as pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Booby traps are hidden devices or pranks set to catch the unwary, a kind of practical joke.

clue.text: Hailstorm breaks out around the East — it's to do with temperature

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are placed around the abbreviation for East
the letters of the storm word break apart and are scattered into a new arrangement

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A weather report: a hailstorm erupts across the eastern region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks out' rearranges HAILSTORM, and 'around' places those letters about E for the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things of equal temperature, as lines on a weather map joining places with the same reading.

clue.text: It may get broken — put it down

definitions.meaning: a best performance that someone may surpass

explanation.surface: Something fragile is set down.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is a best performance that may be broken, and to record is to put down in writing.

clue.text: Respect for a regal method of self-expression

parts.note: the royal 'we', a monarch's way of referring to themselves in the plural

explanation.surface: Admiration is expressed for the way a monarch speaks of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'we', as in Queen Victoria's supposed 'We are not amused', is a monarch speaking of themselves in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential respect mixed with wonder.

clue.text: They gave patient advice on social problems

definitions.text: They gave patient advice on social problems

parts.words: They gave patient advice on social problems
parts.note: patient reads as an adjective, calm and tolerant; really hospital officials who advised patients about their welfare

explanation.surface: Counsellors who calmly advised on society's ills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' seems to mean forbearing; it is the noun, those in hospital. British hospitals once employed these social workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital social workers in Britain were formerly called almoners, advising patients on welfare.

clue.text: Revolutionary Schubert piece

indicators.note: a piece of the composer's name, that is a run of letters inside it, is taken

explanation.surface: A rebellious, groundbreaking composition by the composer Schubert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schubert piece' looks like a musical work; it is a piece cut out of the name itself. 'Revolutionary' is the definition: a wheel's centre is what the revolving parts turn about.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a wheel is the part around which it revolves, so it can be cryptically called revolutionary.

clue.text: It often signalled the start and passing of one's education

definitions.text: It often signalled the start and passing of one's education

parts.words: It often signalled the start and passing of one's education
parts.note: read as a whole life, education's start and end; really the ringing that marked the start of lessons and each change of class through a school day

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look back at what marked the beginning and end of one's schooldays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' suggests completing one's education, but here it is the passing of lessons, each period ending at the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing at school marked the start of the day and the passing of each lesson.

clue.text: Organ that may be vented

parts.note: an abdominal organ that is also the traditional seat of bad temper, so venting it means pouring out anger

explanation.surface: Some body part that can be aired or ventilated.
explanation.walkthrough: To vent one's spleen is to release one's anger; the organ was once thought the seat of ill humour.
explanation.definitionFit: This abdominal organ was held to be the source of bad temper, and its name means anger.

clue.text: Abuse bursts out in private

indicators.note: the three words burst apart and their letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Insults erupt behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts' rearranges the letters of OUT IN PRIVATE; 'out in private' reads as a scene of a private quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: vituperation is bitter verbal abuse or censure.

clue.text: Derelict ship

definitions.meaning: a cargo vessel with no fixed route

explanation.surface: An abandoned vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless vagrant and also a cargo ship with no regular route.

clue.text: Go off with a list

parts.note: to rot is to decay, as food goes off

explanation.surface: Someone leaves taking a list along.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a list of duties and who takes turns at them.

clue.text: Keen to wreck the joint

indicators.note: the letters of the eager word are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone eager to smash up the dive bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like a seedy bar, but it is a body joint; 'to wreck' rearranges KEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: It bores me in the back

indicators.note: the word for me goes inside the word for the back

parts.note: the rear is the back

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a tiresome pain in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It bores me' reads as a tedious thing; 'It bores' alone is the tool, and ME goes 'in' REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reamer is a tool used to enlarge or finish a bored hole.

clue.text: Chaperon needed going round place with a rough reputation

indicators.note: the letters of the escort's word go round into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A chaperon is needed when visiting somewhere with a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' rearranges the letters of CHAPERON. The 'rough reputation' is for seas, not a bad neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern tip of South America is notorious for rough seas and storms that wrecked many ships.

clue.text: Relaxation, say, about a moral slip

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is put about the other pieces

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means when introducing an instance
a sin is a moral lapse

explanation.surface: Unwinding, for instance, after a little moral lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing is a loosening or slackening, a relaxation of tension or rules.

clue.text: Crossing the channel

definitions.meaning: a voyage across water, such as a sea journey
a way through, a corridor or narrow route

explanation.surface: A trip across the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is both a sea journey and a narrow way through, such as a corridor or channel.
